sentences.text: The genus Eosinopteryx contains only one known species, Eosinopteryx brevipenna, which was a very small non-avialan dinosaur measuring about 30 cm in length.
Unlike most troodontids, this creature had a very short snout that was shorter than the diameter of its eye socket.
Eosinopteryx had wings similar in size to Anchiornis huxleyi, with primary feathers longer than the upper arm bone, but an unusual arrangement of wing bones would have prevented flapping motion.

It possessed a very short tail and slender feet lacking the highly curved claws typical of related groups, while the known fossil shows no complex vaned feathers on the tail and the lower legs and feet appear to be featherless.
The species name brevipenna refers to the reduced plumage seen in the type specimen YFGP-T5197.
The genus name Eosinopteryx combines Greek and Latin words meaning "daybreak," "Chinese," and "feather."
The fossil dates to the late Jurassic period (Oxfordian age), approximately 160 million years ago.
Researchers suggest that the discovery of Eosinopteryx indicates the origin of flight was more complex than previously thought.
Comprehensive analyses have classified Eosinopteryx as either a primitive paravian or an avialan, and it belongs to the parent group Paraves.
A 2017 re-evaluation of the Haarlem Archaeopteryx specimen classified Eosinopteryx as an anchiornithid.

Some researchers consider Eosinopteryx to be a junior synonym of Anchiornis, though a 2017 study noted that the tail of Eosinopteryx is incomplete, which invalidates the distinction from Anchiornis based on tail length.
